title: Daisy Bell
description: Harry Dacre's 1892 waltz, "A Bicycle Built for Two", for 2 to 4 singers: the first verse and the chorus, the tune on top in close harmony. A pop song before there were pop songs: a hook everyone knows, and a verse built the way songs still are.

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on the 1892 sheet music's chords. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): the tune's own quick pickup "Of" "a" before "bi-cy-cle", two quavers; where the tune falls to its lowest note, D, on "heart,", "sy," and "dart," the alto sings F sharp, a third above it, so the duet keeps the D7 chord's third, and likewise it sings B a third above the tune's G on "Bell!" and stays on G, a third above, where the tune falls to E on "not," and "lot"; the alto follows the tune's own leaps a third under it, F sharp up to B and down to G on "sy, Dai-sy!", and B, G on "bi-cy-" after resting through "Of a"; and its fall of a fifth from F sharp on "Bell!" to B on the chorus's first "Dai-" comes across the breath into the chorus, then turns back up a third to D on "sy,".
licence.source: Daisy Bell, song, written and composed by Harry Dacre (T. B. Harms & Co., New York, and Francis, Day & Hunter, London, copyright 1892), pp. 3 to 5: the voice line, verse 1 and the chorus, in G; read from the scan at archive.org/details/daisybell00harr
